headline: Attackers took root on Check Point gateways and wiped VMware ESXi hosts while Microsoft spent a second day hunting the cause of a worldwide Microsoft 365 outage.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers now go after the devices that guard and manage everything else, chaining PHP2Shell on Check Point Security Gateways to root and erasing VMware ESXi files while N-central zero-days turn managed service providers into a delivery route.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Check Point Gateways Fall to PHP2Shell and a Gaia OS Bug

emerging_trends.text: One supplier's bad day becomes every customer's: ransomware at ActiveCloud froze Belarusian businesses for days, Apify lost customer data and stored secrets, and TSMC traced leaked employee records to a cloud service provider it uses.

topics.title: Check Point Gateways Fall to PHP2Shell and a Gaia OS Bug
topics.latest_developments: Check Point shipped emergency hotfixes on November 13, 2026 for a high-severity flaw attackers have exploited since late October to take root and hold persistence, and the company detailed a campaign that started October 30, 2026 against Israeli organizations: an unidentified actor entered unpatched Security Gateways through the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, escalated to root with CVE-2026-123039, a previously unreported local privilege escalation in Gaia OS, installed a backdoor named TSGA, and ran data-wiping malware against connected VMware ESXi hosts, with a wider wave following; Citrix separately closed 10 critical NetScaler vulnerabilities that drive unexpected behavior and denial of service.
topics.summary: Check Point Security Gateways sit at the perimeter of enterprise networks and route all traffic through Gaia OS. Administrators should install the hotfixes immediately, hunt for TSGA, and check ESXi datastores for deleted files.

topics.title: Microsoft 365 Outage Enters a Second Day
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft kept working the worldwide Microsoft 365 outage through November 13, 2026, telling customers it is taking "a measured approach to identify and repair affected infrastructure" and trying several routes to find the cause, a day after Outlook, Exchange Online, Teams, and Copilot cut out for business and enterprise customers; the company points to failed server health checks and elevated loads and reports no evidence of a cyberattack, while Wired counted businesses, schools, hospitals, and governments learning the cost of running their work on one company's systems.
topics.summary: The failure hit the mail, meeting, and assistant services that most large companies run their day on, and it left staff whose jobs consist of email unable to send any. Operations teams should keep an out-of-band communication channel ready and watch for phishing that impersonates outage notices.

topics.title: November Windows Updates Break Printing and Activation
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft confirmed on November 13, 2026 that the November 2026 Patch Tuesday updates fail Windows activation and licensing with 0x80041008 errors, and warned earlier in the week that the same updates may break printing of documents carrying complex formatting; researchers meanwhile spelled out the mechanism of SignDrop, the unpatched Windows zero-day exploit that Abdelhamid Naceri, who goes by Nightmare Eclipse, published this week in frustration with Microsoft, which abuses the Common Log File System driver and Windows Defender to create arbitrary files in the antimalware process's context and hand a local user SYSTEM rights.
topics.summary: The November release closed more than 1,200 flaws, including the exploited Outlook zero-day CVE-2026-124194, so skipping it carries real risk. Administrators should stage the rollout, keep a licensing and printing rollback plan ready, and track Microsoft's release health notes for the fixes.

topics.title: North Korea Runs Fake Zoom Calls and Fake Engineers
topics.latest_developments: The FBI put the FaceStealer scheme at more than $400 million in cryptocurrency stolen over 18 months, said it has seized more than 900 webcam recordings the operators replay to make fake Zoom and Microsoft Teams calls look real, and warned cryptocurrency and web3 employees plus open-source maintainers on November 12, 2026; Material Security reported the same week that it tracked 27 fabricated North Korean job-seeker personas through the hiring pipelines of organizations it monitors all the way to onboarding over one year, and that one company a persona reached in the past month kept roughly 277,000 files holding Social Security numbers open to everyone in the company or to anyone with a public link; and Dark Reading reported that the crew behind the $1.2 billion Binance theft worked a known weakness and absent controls, with attacker-deployed sweeper contracts blunting the exchange's damage limits.
topics.summary: North Korean operators infect a target during a video call that shows stolen footage of earlier victims, then drain wallets, and they also apply for remote engineering jobs under invented identities. Companies hiring remote engineers should verify identity documents against live video and lock down company-wide file sharing before onboarding anyone.

topics.title: Operation TorNado Arrests 354 Dark Web Traders
topics.latest_developments: Europol and police in 14 countries arrested 354 dark web vendors and buyers in Operation TorNado, which ran from May 2025 to October 2026 and worked backward from five marketplaces already taken offline—Archetyp, Bohemia, Nemesis, Kingdom, and Tor2Door—as well as forums and single-vendor shops; investigators put this week's Operation Endgame round at 235 servers and 257 domains seized behind Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC, with 6.4 million stolen logins recovered from more than 40,000 victims, according to Germany's Federal Criminal Police Office; and Justice Department officials briefed reporters on November 13, 2026 that Gootloader served at least 44 ransomware attacks costing $29 million since 2018.
topics.summary: Both operations show that a marketplace or botnet takedown leaves a usable evidence trail against the people who traded on it. Organizations should assume credentials harvested by StealC and Gootloader circulate now and force resets on accounts appearing in the recovered sets.

topics.title: Ransomware Strands a Belarusian Cloud as Apify Loses Data
topics.latest_developments: ActiveCloud, the Belarusian cloud provider, said hackers breached its systems and encrypted parts of its cloud infrastructure, cutting customers off from key services for several days; Apify, the web scraping company, confirmed on November 13, 2026 that an intruder reached customer accounts and took personal information and stored data; TSMC, the Taiwanese chipmaker, confirmed the same day that stolen employee data matched records held in the system services of a cloud service provider it uses and said no TSMC system fell; and British organizations have filed a record number of cyber incident reports with the country's data protection regulator this year, a surge security firms attribute to data extortion and AI-assisted attacks.
topics.summary: A single hosting or data-platform compromise takes every tenant's service and stored secrets with it, and the reporting numbers show the pace rising. Companies should inventory which suppliers hold their credentials and data, demand breach notification terms, and rehearse operating without each one.

topics.title: ClickFix Lures Wear Zillow, Teams, and AI Brands
topics.latest_developments: The SANS Internet Storm Center documented Macfinger, a ClickFix campaign that pushes the DownTheDRAIN infostealer onto macOS, which extends the pattern three other teams reported this week: EfficientIP Research Labs traced ClickFix pages dressed as Zillow apartment reviews that copied a PowerShell command to the visitor's clipboard behind a routine-looking verification check and installed NetSupport RAT with its window hidden and a restart at every login; the browser security company Island counted 186 lookalike domains impersonating AI tools, a pattern it calls TypoPrompting, serving the same verification lures plus browser-hijacking malware and search-hijacking extensions; and Huntress documented attackers who used a fake Microsoft Teams meeting scheduler to talk an employee at a construction company into typing a device code into Microsoft's genuine sign-in page, which handed them a valid session token before the Huntress security operations center caught it.
topics.summary: All of these campaigns ask the victim to perform one normal-looking step—paste a command, enter a code—and that step delivers remote access, an infostealer, or a session token. Blocking clipboard-to-shell execution on Windows and macOS, disabling the device code sign-in flow where business needs allow, and filtering lookalike AI domains cut off the common path.

topics.title: N-able Restricts N-central as Agent2Shell Spreads
topics.latest_developments: N-able said on Thursday, November 12, 2026 that it is restricting certain N-central features and integrations while remediation continues, after a researcher published a second flaw set named Agent2Shell alongside 4EverAble2Shell, the zero-day that lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker run code as root and that attackers turned on within hours of the proof of concept, planting cryptocurrency miners on at least 21 servers, 19 of them running the company's newest hotfix.
topics.summary: N-central manages endpoints for managed service providers, so one compromised server reaches every customer network it touches. Operators should apply the hotfixes, keep the Legacy API off and off the public internet, and hunt for miners and new root accounts.

topics.title: SilentAir Intercepts SMS Codes Inside Asian Carriers
topics.latest_developments: Enea, the Stockholm telecommunications and cybersecurity software company, named a new espionage group SilentAir this week, reporting that it hijacks network nodes inside Asian mobile operators to intercept the calls and text messages of selected people, most of them Taiwanese subscribers, and that its attack sources trace to at least six Asian countries; Enea assesses with high confidence that a state runs it.
topics.summary: SilentAir reads traffic from inside carrier networks, which hands it the one-time codes that SMS two-factor authentication delivers. Any organization protecting accounts with text-message codes should move high-value users to hardware keys or app-based authentication.

sources.title: SilentAir Hijacks Asian Telecom Networks to Intercept SMS 2FA Codes and Spy on Taiwanese Users

topics.title: Germany Grants Spies Hacking Powers as Attackers Hit a Drone Maker
topics.latest_developments: The Bundestag passed a bill on November 13, 2026 by 308 votes to 190, with 71 abstentions, that hands German intelligence agencies hacking and sabotage powers, the largest rewrite of the country's spy laws since the war and the product of a draft Chancellor Friedrich Merz's cabinet approved months earlier; the same day, Quantum Systems, the German defense technology company whose aircraft fly for the German military, confirmed it caught an incident in late October that formed part of an active cyberattack by what it called hostile actors, and the attack disrupted military drone operations.
topics.summary: Germany now lets its intelligence services break into systems and conduct sabotage, a step its parliament debated for months, while its drone supply chain absorbs an active attack. Defense suppliers and their subcontractors should expect state-level targeting and verify that they detect intrusions in production and flight-operations systems.

business_politics.latest_developments: Crude rose for a third session Friday, November 13, and still headed for a weekly loss as traders weighed the International Energy Agency's finding, published the same morning, that the global oil market returns to surplus in the fourth quarter for the first time since the Iran war began, and United States natural gas futures pulled back after government data showed inventories rising by more than usual last week.

team_usa.title: Naeher Retires After 16 Years
team_usa.latest_developments: Alyssa Naeher announced her retirement from professional soccer Friday, November 13, closing a 16-year career.
team_usa.summary: Naeher kept goal for the Chicago Stars of the National Women's Soccer League and for the United States women's national team, and ESPN calls her a legend of both. Her exit leaves the next United States coaching staff to settle a goalkeeping depth chart before the Concacaf W Championship.

team_usa.title: Girma's Fitness Clouds the W Championship
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN reported Friday, November 13, that United States defender Naomi Girma remains a fitness concern for the Concacaf W Championship later this month, a tournament that doubles as a World Cup decider.
team_usa.summary: Girma, who plays for Chelsea in England, has carried fitness problems through the season, and she anchors the United States women's national team back line. Her availability shapes how the Americans line up in the matches that settle their World Cup qualification.

sources.title: USWNT's Girma in doubt for World Cup decider amid ongoing fitness concerns

team_usa.title: Pochettino Agrees to Manage Manchester United
team_usa.latest_developments: Manchester United confirmed Mauricio Pochettino as its head coach Friday, November 13, and U.S. Soccer said he leaves the United States men's national team on November 17, with Steve Cherundolo running the December camp on an interim basis; a tearful Pochettino called the departure the toughest decision of his career.
team_usa.summary: Pochettino replaces Michael Carrick, whom Manchester United sacked Thursday, November 12, with the team in the relegation zone. ESPN's reckoning of his United States tenure describes real highs shadowed by a mercenary feel and an eye on a return to Europe, and ESPN's transfer reporting has United looking at two of his American internationals, AS Monaco striker Folarin Balogun and defender Alex Freeman.

team_usa.title: Rapinoe, Altidore, and Ertz Enter the Hall of Fame
team_usa.latest_developments: The National Soccer Hall of Fame elected Megan Rapinoe, Jozy Altidore, and Julie Ertz on Thursday, November 12, all on the first ballot, and David Beckham also won election.
team_usa.summary: Rapinoe and Ertz anchored the United States women's national teams that won the 2015 and 2019 World Cups, and Altidore scored 42 goals for the men's national team across more than a decade. The class puts three recently retired American internationals into the hall in a single vote.
